_about: Permanent register of every published Briefings sector report. One entry per published sector — add an entry here when a sector's status in the AI Landscape sector-report-tracker.md moves to Published. The briefings.html page reads this file directly (no live feed, unlike the Practice Library — these are not Substack posts). 'image' is optional — a card thumbnail from the sector's Data Poster series (gold/Cormorant sub-brand); cards render fine without one.
_aboutCollaborations: Second, separate register for briefings co-authored with a named industry practitioner — same card fields as 'briefings' above, plus two more: 'collaboratorName' (required to trigger the byline) and 'collaboratorTitle' (optional, appended after a comma — e.g. 'Head of Claims Transformation, XYZ Insurance'). Rendered in its own Collaborations section on briefings.html with its own empty-state copy. Add an entry here, not to 'briefings', when a collaboration is published.

briefings.title: AI in UK Insurance Claims
briefings.standfirst: Claims costs are at record levels, the regulator has named claims handling its top priority for 2026, and the first AI-fabricated claims are already on the record.
briefings.imageAlt: The first mover on AI in UK claims wasn't the insurer — 95% of insurers already use AI, 46% report only partial understanding, £174m in fraud cases combatted

briefings.title: AI in UK Social Housing
briefings.standfirst: Awaab's Law starts a legal clock the moment a landlord becomes aware of a hazard. The regulator, the Ombudsman and the sector's own flagship AI case study all say the constraint is data, not technology.
briefings.imageAlt: It doesn't ask what you fixed, it asks what you knew — 30 Nov Awaab's Law Phase 2, +43% Ombudsman property-condition findings, 31% of staff using AI vs 22% given access

briefings.title: AI in UK Construction & Building Safety
briefings.standfirst: The golden thread is a legal duty with no named technical standard attached to it. The standard the duty needs already exists — ISO 19650, seven years in the making — and is compelled for public sector clients and optional for everyone else. 74% of architecture professionals use BIM; 36% describe that as conforming to the standard.
briefings.humanMoment: The golden thread and the gateway approval
briefings.imageAlt: Most of the industry has the tool. Far fewer have the discipline — 74% of architecture professionals using BIM against 36% describing it as ISO 19650 conformance, and 37% of the construction products market regulated on the government's own central estimate

briefings.title: AI in UK Energy Retail
briefings.standfirst: Satisfaction is at a record high and complaints at their lowest since 2022, while debt hits £4.79bn and arrears without a repayment plan run at three times managed debt. Ofgem has twice this year found the customer record itself unreliable — and that record is what an AI system would learn from.
briefings.humanMoment: Self-disconnection on a smart prepayment meter
briefings.imageAlt: Every service measure is improving. Every measure of debt is getting worse — 82% satisfaction, £4.79bn debt and arrears, 48% Ombudsman signposting rate

briefings.title: AI in UK Grocery Retail
briefings.standfirst: Four regulators hold a position on AI in or around this sector and none is aimed at its largest deployments. Facial recognition is reaching around two hundred stores on the strength of a two-store trial, while machine learning forecasting already sits inside a statutory duty requiring due care, consultation and an explainable basis.
briefings.humanMoment: The tap on the shoulder at the self-checkout
briefings.imageAlt: Every regulator has a position. None of them is aimed here — five ICO priorities with retail not among them, zero mentions of technology or AI across two 2026 Groceries Code Adjudicator publications, and Sainsbury's facial recognition going from two stores to around two hundred

briefings.title: AI in UK BioTech
briefings.standfirst: UK biotech venture investment hit a five-year high in Q2 2026. One company's round accounts for three quarters of it, the MHRA is now receiving AI-drafted inspection responses that cite guidance which doesn't exist, and four named companies' outcomes over two years run from a verified drug-discovery success to outright absorption into a US competitor.
briefings.humanMoment: The named signature on an AI-drafted inspection response
briefings.imageAlt: One deal made the quarter a record. Three companies complicate it — £2.05bn in UK biotech venture investment against £498m excluding the one deal, and $2.9bn in combined milestone potential behind Isomorphic Labs' two pharma deals

briefings.title: AI in UK HealthTech
briefings.standfirst: The same AI ambient-voice product was measured twice in 2026 — once by the NHS as a productivity gain, once by the regulator as a source of undetected errors. The £10bn rollout is built on the first measurement, and nothing yet exists to count what the second one found.
briefings.humanMoment: The clinician who has stopped reading the note before signing it
briefings.imageAlt: The NHS measured the time it saved. The regulator measured what it missed — 23.5% relative increase in direct care time against 39% of real-world notes flagged out-of-scope by the MHRA's own sandbox

briefings.title: AI in UK Policing & Public Safety
briefings.standfirst: Policing is nationalising the capability faster than it is nationalising the accountability. A national AI centre, a national facial recognition system and national procurement are funded and moving, while the legal framework is, on the Home Secretary's own account, still being refined.
briefings.humanMoment: The stop, and the custody decision
briefings.imageAlt: Bought nationally, answered for locally — £75m for a national AI centre over three years, 43 territorial forces each answering to a locally elected commissioner, and more than 25,000 retrospective facial recognition searches a month

briefings.title: AI in UK Banking & Consumer Lending
briefings.standfirst: The regulator has decided not to write rules for AI and has said so in terms. That decision has already moved the accountability onto named individuals under the Senior Managers regime — against the regulators' own finding that 46 per cent of firms only partly understand the AI systems they are running.
briefings.humanMoment: The affordability decline and the arrears call
briefings.imageAlt: The sector adopted it, then told the regulator it did not understand it — 75% of firms already using AI, 46% reporting only partial understanding, and one in three use cases bought in from third parties

briefings.title: AI in UK Legal Services
briefings.standfirst: The one sector where the regulator can count the harm — 42 reports of potential AI misuse in twelve months. Every referral the courts actually made was about supervision, not about the technology, and the service gap driving firms to buy lands on the same junior review layer.
briefings.humanMoment: The filing, the disclosure exercise, the cited case
briefings.imageAlt: The tools got better, the supervision requirement did not move — 42 reports of potential AI misuse counted by the regulator, a best benchmark score rising from 4.4 to 6.4 out of ten, and a 37% rise in complaints to the Legal Ombudsman

briefings.title: AI in UK Justice, Courts & Probation
briefings.standfirst: Justice has filed twelve algorithmic transparency records, including an exemplary one for a prison violence estimator. Search the same register for the scoring that helps decide recall and release, and it returns nothing — while the department's own revalidation reports miscalibration by ethnicity.
briefings.imageAlt: The new tools are on the register, the ones that score you are not — 152 records on the transparency register, 12 from the justice family, 0 returned for OASys, recidivism or parole

briefings.title: AI in UK Mortgages & Housing Finance
briefings.standfirst: The FCA's own research shows a machine-learning model ranks borrowers better; its own consultation describes a borrower declined automatically by a filter. From 1 January 2027, Basel 3.1 makes keeping every home's valuation current a standing duty — and the largest lenders say nothing about AI in the mortgage decision.
briefings.humanMoment: The automatic decline and the forbearance decision
briefings.imageAlt: The regulator's model ranks borrowers better, its own case study was declined by a filter — an AUC of 0.751 for the machine-learning model against 0.669 for the conventional one, and a 74 per cent higher arrears hazard above 90 per cent loan-to-value

briefings.title: AI in UK Pensions & Retirement Income
briefings.standfirst: The FCA says it remains comfortable AI can work inside targeted support, a regime built for groups of people. The Pensions Regulator is building defaults to protect members from biased or flawed AI-powered advice. 69.4 per cent of first pension accesses happen without advice.
briefings.imageAlt: One decision, two regulators, two answers on AI — 961,575 pension pots accessed for the first time in 2024/25, 69.4 per cent without regulated advice, against 112,000 Pension Wise appointments in the same year

briefings.title: AI in UK Wealth & Investment Advice
briefings.standfirst: The FCA proposes replacing the annual suitability review with needs-based reviews, and says firms can use technology to assess suitability on an ongoing basis. The review is what 3.7 million clients pay for — and two of the largest advice firms are still remediating reviews they could not evidence.
briefings.imageAlt: The annual review is going and the FCA says technology can decide when — 3.7 million clients pay for ongoing advice, ongoing services are 80 per cent of adviser-charge revenue, and 83 per cent of reviews were delivered across 22 large firms

collaborations.title: When the Model Said It Was Fine
collaborations.standfirst: The US has just excluded agentic AI from its flagship model risk framework. European supervisors have answered by restating the frameworks they already have. A joint examination of the discipline financial services built to govern models — and why, on its own terms, it no longer reaches what AI now deploys.
collaborations.humanMoment: The named signature on the annual MRM attestation
